What each table is called, which fields it shows, and the actions, forms, access and rules that belong to it. **Preview** keys work and may change in any release ([status](/docs/status/)); the rest are stable. [All parts](/docs/app-dsl/).

```ts
resources: {
  opportunity: {
    access: 'write',
    display: { amount: { format: 'money' }, stage: { tone: { closed_won: 'good', closed_lost: 'bad' } } },
    form: { show: ['name', 'account_id', ['amount', 'close_date']], defaults: { stage: 'prospecting' } },
    actions: { markWon: action('Mark won', { set: { stage: 'closed_won' }, when: 'stage = negotiation' }) },
    computed: { is_stale: computed.boolean('close_date < today and stage != closed_won') },
  },
  account: {},
},
```

Every table a view, dashboard or page reads needs a block, and `{}` is
enough: an App serves only its declared resources, and every declared
resource reads. Only `access: 'write'` writes, and the connection's
`"writable": true` still applies ([Resources and fields](/docs/access-model/)).
A resource's name is bare for the default source and `source.name` for
another. Every yes/no key takes `true` or `false`, and `false` means what
leaving it out means.

## Rollups

```ts
account: {
  rollups: {
    open_deals: count('opportunity', { query: 'stage != closed_won and stage != closed_lost' }),
    open_pipeline: sum('opportunity', 'amount', { query: 'stage != closed_won and stage != closed_lost' }),
  },
},
```

`count`, `sum`, `min` and `max` read the rows that point at the record, and
`latest` reads a column of the newest of them: an order's
`financial_status: latest('payment', 'status')` is its payment's own word,
read where the payment writes it, so no command keeps a copy on the order in
step (newest by key, or by `by`, a date). A
rollup reads like a column in `show`, sorts, tabs, conditions, a command's
`when`, cards and measures, and through a reference (`account_id.open_deals`). It reaches two
hops (`whose: 'task_id.project_id'`), `latest` included: a customer's
`last_service: latest('work_order', 'status', { whose: 'bike_id.customer_id' })` is the newest
of all their bikes' orders. It is computed in the same statement under
the grants and row policy of every table it walks, and is never written. Not
on API sources. Its `query` may follow the rows' references, so a product's
units sold leave out cancelled orders without a status copied onto each line:
`sum('order_line', 'quantity', { whose: 'variant_id.product_id', query: 'sales_order_id.status != cancelled' })`.

## Segments

```ts
work_order: {
  segments: {
    open: 'status is open',
    overdue: { query: 'open and due_on < today', label: 'Late' },
  },
},
```

A segment names a query once. Its name is a word of the query language
(`overdue and mine`), a tab names it (`tabs: ['open', { segment: 'overdue', sort: 'due_on' }]`),
a section takes it as its source (`metric('Late', 'work_order.overdue')`,
`related(..., { segment: 'open' })`), and a rollup counts it
(`count('work_order', { segment: 'open' })`). A tab's label and its address
(`?tab=overdue`) are the segment's. A segment may name another, never in a
loop, and a name a column, rollup or state already holds is refused. It only
ever narrows: a reader who may not read a column it names is served no tab,
section or word for it. The App API and MCP list it read-only as
`?segment=overdue`. `check --design` lists each segment with its cost, and
warns where one query is written in several places (`repeated-query`).

## Stock a line uses

```ts
work_order_part: {
  consumes: { column: 'part_id.on_hand', by: 'quantity', refuse: 'Only {part_id.on_hand} of {part_id.name} left' },
},
```

A line that uses stock moves the balance on every write, through every door: a
new line takes `by` (one, without it), a removed line gives it back, an edit
moves the difference, and a line moved to another part gives back to one and
takes from the other. A take past zero refuses the whole write as
`consumes_refused`, with `refuse` filled from the part as it stands and only
with what the reader may read; `floor: false` allows a backorder. Writing the
line is the whole grant: no role needs to write `on_hand`. A stored balance
that must refuse an oversell is `consumes`; a figure that is only read is a
rollup. `check` warns when a command also writes the balance
(`consumes-written`).

## Row-defined fields

```ts
product: { defined: { specs: { from: 'attribute', per: 'category_id' } } },
attribute: { access: 'write', delete: true },
```

A JSON column whose keys are rows people keep: each row of `from` has `key`,
`label` and `type` (`text`, `textarea`, `number`, `money`, `date`,
`datetime`, `bool`, `choice`, `choices`), and may have `options` (one per
line), `required`, `help` and `position`. With `per`, a record gets the rows
whose `per` equals its own and those whose `per` is empty. The fields are
drawn on record pages and forms as the record's own, judged at the server
in the write's transaction (a refusal names `specs.capacity`), read in the
tenant's scope, asked by a list as `specs.capacity`, and offered one facet
each where a view's `filters` names the column. PostgreSQL and SQLite.

## Computed columns

```ts
task: {
  computed: {
    is_overdue: computed.boolean('due_on < today and not completed'),
    days_open: computed.number('today - opened_on'),
    renews_on: computed.date('ends_on + term months'),
  },
},
```

An expression in the query language's words: columns and paths, rollups,
numbers, quoted text, `today`, `now`, `me`, comparisons, `and`, `or`, `not`,
`is empty`, `+ - * /` (a division by zero has no value), date spans, and five
functions: `coalesce(a, b, …)` (the first with a value), `round(x)` or
`round(x, 2)` (a half away from zero), `abs(x)`, and `min(a, b, …)` and
`max(a, b, …)` of numbers or dates, which have no value where one of theirs has
none (`computed.number('max(owed - paid, 0)')`). It is
written into the statement, so it shows, sorts, filters and tones like a
column, and a rollup sums it (`sum('task', 'overrun')`) or a dashboard
window reads a computed date (`over: 'renews_on'`) when it reads only its
row's own columns; it is never written, and `fields.write`, `form.show` and an action's
`set` refuse it. A role is served it only where every column it reads is
readable to that role. A fixed action's `set` takes the same kind of
expression for a stamp (`computed.date('today + 14 days')`); anything heavier
is a [command](/docs/commands/) or a database view.

## Unions

```ts
import { union } from '@mistriwork/mistri/app';

unions: [
  union('my_requests', [
    { from: 'incident', as: { title: 'short_description', opened: 'opened_at' } },
    { from: 'requested_item', as: { title: 'name', opened: 'created_at' } },
  ]),
],
```

One read-only list over tables that share a shape. A list view and `useRows`
name it as they name a table, in one order and one page; each row also says
`from` and `key`, and opens its own record. Each branch is read under the
reader's own grants and row policy, so a branch they cannot read is none of
their rows. A union lists; it has no record page, breakdown or summary.

## Record names and conditions

```ts
purchase_order: { recordLabel: 'PO-{id}' },
po_line: { recordLabel: '{product_id.name} × {qty}' },
```

`recordLabel` is a column, a label path or a template in braces, computed in
SQL so lists, pickers and breadcrumbs sort and search the same name.

Every condition (a list's `query`, a tab, a section's `query`, a `when`, a
validation's `must`) is [the query language](/docs/query/). `me` is the
signed-in person: their email beside a text column, or their row beside a
reference once `auth.me` says where people live. `me.<table>.<column>` is
their memberships: `team_id in (me.team_member.team_id)` is the rows of the
teams they are in, read on each request through their own rows (the one
column of `team_member` that points at people says whose; at most 1,000).
Where nobody is signed in to be it (the database browser, MCP, the App API, a
rollup), `me` is refused rather than read as the word; quote it (`"me"`) to
mean the text. A path walks references
(`product_id.unit_cost > 50`). Another column is compared by naming it on the
right: a path always, a bare word beside a number, date or flag
(`shipped_on > promised_on`); beside text a bare word is a value.

## Validation

```ts
validation: [
  { must: 'close_date >= created_on', message: 'A deal cannot close before it was created.' },
  { must: 'probability = 100', when: 'stage = closed_won', message: 'A won deal is at 100% probability.' },
],
```

A rule is a condition the record must meet on every write, optionally under
`when`, which compares the record's own columns. At most 128 rules per
resource.

## `resources`

| Key | Type | Status | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `resources` | object | Stable | One block per logical resource, keyed bare for the default source or source.name for a secondary one. Used in `examples/apps/tick/app.ts`. |

## `resources.*.access`

| Key | Type | Status | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `resources.*.access` | `"write"` | Stable | The App's ceiling for this resource. An App serves only its declared resources, and a declared one reads; say 'write' for one the App writes. With auth.roles, roles grant within the ceilings. One of `write`. Used in `examples/apps/tick/app.ts`. |

## `resources.*.actions`

| Key | Type | Status | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `resources.*.actions` | object | Stable | What may be done to one record, keyed by its id and drawn in the order written: defined once and offered wherever the records appear — on record pages, in a queue (the bulk ones, for a selection), on a board (updates that set exactly its by). A header's primary and destructive, a queue's actions and a role's actions name one by its id. Used in `examples/apps/tick/app.ts`. |
| `resources.*.actions.*.bulk` | boolean | Stable | May run on a selection, App-wide: a queue offers it for its selection. A fixed update is one ordinary write per selected record, with results per record; a command must declare targets: many and runs the whole selection as one atomic request. |
| `resources.*.actions.*.command` | string | Stable | A command, by its name in the App's commands module (defineCommands). The server fills in its input, target and version from the registration; mistri-commands.d.ts types the names. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/app.ts`. |
| `resources.*.actions.*.confirm` | boolean | Stable | Ask before writing. A command that asks nothing runs on one click unless it confirms; a command with inputs asks them in its form, which is its confirmation, and is refused one. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/resources.ts`. |
| `resources.*.actions.*.header` | boolean | Stable | false keeps the button out of the record's action bar and its menu, for a verb the App runs from its own place: a custom component through useCommand, a queue's selection, a board's lane. Still granted, judged and run as before; a record header that names it is refused. Default `true`. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/blueprint.ts`. |
| `resources.*.actions.*.inputs` | object | Stable | A command action's input drawn by the App's own input component (kind 'input'), in its form. An input in a group is named by its path (trade.vin), and in a repeating group stands in every row. |
| `resources.*.actions.*.inputs.*.kind` |  | Stable |  One of `input`. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/blueprint.ts`. |
| `resources.*.actions.*.label` | string | Stable |  |
| `resources.*.actions.*.reason` | string | Stable | A column this action asks a reason for and writes with its set. Required when the action runs; not with bulk or a command. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/resources.ts`. |
| `resources.*.actions.*.set` | object | Stable | Column → value the action writes: a literal, or a value the server works out in the write — { "auto": "now" } (the constant now: a DATE gets the day in ui.timezone, else UTC; a TIMESTAMP or DATETIME with no zone the wall clock in ui.timezone (UTC without one), one with a zone (timestamptz) the UTC instant), { "auto": "today" } (the App's day, into a DATE), { "auto": "me" } (the constant me: the signed-in account's email, into a text column of an App with auth), or a constant expression in the computed-column grammar, { "type": "date", "value": "today + 14 days" } (computed.date('today + 14 days')), which reads no column and fits its column's type. The text "now", "today" or "me", and text starting with "=", is refused, since it would read as one of those. Used in `examples/apps/tick/app.ts`. |
| `resources.*.actions.*.set.*.auto` | `"today"` · `"now"` · `"me"` | Stable |  One of `me`, `now`, `today`. |
| `resources.*.actions.*.set.*.type` | `"boolean"` · `"number"` · `"date"` | Stable |  One of `boolean`, `date`, `number`. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/blueprint.ts`. |
| `resources.*.actions.*.set.*.value` | string | Stable | A constant expression: numbers, true, false, today, now, me, comparisons, and, or, not, + - * /, and date spans (today + 14 days, now + 1 week). No column. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/views.ts`. |
| `resources.*.actions.*.when` | string | Stable | Shown only when the record matches, in the query language. Used in `examples/apps/tick/app.ts`. |

| Key | Type | Status | What it does |

| `resources.*.computed` | object | Stable | Virtual columns, each a typed expression over the record's own columns in the query language's words, with today, now and me: { is_overdue: { type: 'boolean', value: 'due_on &lt; today and not completed' } }; hours and minutes move an instant (now - 30 minutes, due_at - 2 hours). Used in `examples/apps/lintel/views.ts`. |

Left out, an App sets a key, a reference, a code or a QR value in the data face and any other text in the reading face. A rule with a component takes no face, the component sets its own; masked: true takes none either. One of `code`, `data`, `ui`. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/blueprint.ts`. |
| `resources.*.display.*.format` | `"money"` · `"percent"` · `"number"` · `"relative"` · `"items"` · `"duration"` · `"email"` · `"phone"` · `"url"` · `"richText"` · `"avatars"` · `"rating"` · `"color"` · `"time"` · `"month"` · `"year"` · `"json"` · `"qr"` | Stable | money: currency formatting (metrics compact to "$27.9M"). percent: the value is 0–100, shown with %. number: separators forced on. relative: a date said from today ("in 3 days", "64 days ago"), the date itself in the tooltip. items: a text of one item per line, drawn as a list (a line of them where there is no room). duration: a number of seconds said as its two largest units ("2h 15m"), the seconds in the tooltip. email, phone, url: a value of that shape is a link to write to, call or open; an App links a column named like one without a rule. richText: sanitized HTML, drawn formatted on a record and as an excerpt in a list, edited in the rich text editor; the server sanitizes every write and reads Markdown into it. avatars: the people on a thing (an array, a JSON array, or one name per line or comma) as up to three overlapping initials discs and a "+N"; takes nothing else. rating: a whole number of stars out of outOf (5). color: a hex color as its swatch and code. time, month, year: a time of day, a month, a year in the reader's words, each edited in its native picker. json: a JSON document as a tree, edited as text whose problem is said while it is typed; the server refuses a write that is not JSON. qr: the value as a QR code to scan. These draw the value their own way. One of `avatars`, `color`, `duration`, `email`, `items`, `json`, `money`, `month`, `number`, `percent`, `phone`, `qr`, `rating`, `relative`, `richText`, `time`, `url`, `year`. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/resources.ts`. |

## `resources.*.file`

| Key | Type | Status | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `resources.*.file` | object | Stable | The rows are files: content names the binary column holding the bytes (BLOB, bytea), name the file name; type and size, when named, are filled from the upload; thumbnail names a smaller copy for cards. A related list over the resource draws as attachments, uploading where the reader may add a row (its create names the label). maxBytes caps an upload (10 MB when unsaid, at most 25 MB). In a row-policy App an upload is an insert the policy judges, and removing a file a delete. A tenant App reads and uploads its files on the tenant's lease, each at most 10 MB, and only its own tenant's. storage 'bucket' keeps new files' bytes in an S3-compatible bucket (AWS S3, R2, MinIO, B2, Tigris), the row naming the object in its object column; the server's MISTRI_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID and MISTRI_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY sign every request, and the server does not start without them. object and hash need no grant: a reader of content reads the file, and they are the server's alone, sent to no browser and named by no request, App API or MCP tool. An upload is one request, so maxBytes stays at most 25 MB with a bucket; multipart upload is not supported. mistri migrate files moves files to where storage says and sweeps objects no row names; an App served with jobs is swept daily by the server, a tenant App tenant by tenant. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/resources.ts`. |
| `resources.*.file.bucket` | object | Stable | An S3-compatible bucket the files' bytes are kept in: its address only, the credentials being the server's environment. |
| `resources.*.file.bucket.endpoint` | string | Stable | The service's address, for any but AWS: https://&lt;account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com, or a local one such as `http://localhost:9000`. |
| `resources.*.file.bucket.name` | string | Stable | The bucket's name. Used in `examples/apps/tick/app.ts`. |
| `resources.*.file.bucket.pathStyle` | boolean | Stable | true addresses the bucket as a path (&lt;endpoint>/&lt;name>/&lt;key>), as MinIO wants; otherwise as a host. |
| `resources.*.file.bucket.prefix` | string | Stable | A folder every key goes under, so Apps can share one bucket. |
| `resources.*.file.bucket.presign` | boolean | Stable | true sends a download straight from the bucket, by a redirect to a URL signed for a minute; otherwise it passes through the server. |
| `resources.*.file.bucket.region` | string | Stable | Its region: us-east-1 when unsaid; auto for R2. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/pages/maintenance_request.ts`. |
| `resources.*.file.content` | string | Stable |  Used in `examples/apps/lintel/resources.ts`. |
| `resources.*.file.hash` | string | Stable | A text column the upload fills with the file's SHA-256 (hex), which tags it for caches. The server's alone: granted with content, named by no request. |
| `resources.*.file.maxBytes` | integer | Stable |  Used in `examples/apps/lintel/resources.ts`. |
| `resources.*.file.name` | string | Stable |  Used in `examples/apps/tick/app.ts`. |
| `resources.*.file.object` | string | Stable | A text column naming each file's object in the bucket; null for a file kept in content. The server's alone: granted with content, named by no request. |
| `resources.*.file.size` | string | Stable |  Used in `examples/apps/lintel/blueprint.ts`. |
| `resources.*.file.storage` | `"database"` · `"bucket"` | Stable | Where new files' bytes go: database (when unsaid) or bucket. A file is read from wherever its row says. One of `bucket`, `database`. |
| `resources.*.file.thumbnail` | string | Stable | A binary column holding a smaller copy of each file's picture, which cards and gallery strips draw instead of the whole file. Whoever writes the row fills it (a seed, an import); a row without one is drawn from the file itself. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/resources.ts`. |
| `resources.*.file.type` | string | Stable |  Used in `examples/apps/lintel/blueprint.ts`. |

A notify step tells the audience a notify rule names with on: { flow }. Steps sharing a position start together and join; a run keeps the rows it started with. A jobs module's flowRunner runs them on this resource's records, durably; a step of an App kind runs one of the App's commands on the record. |

Besides a literal, three constants: today on a date column, now on a date-and-time column, and me (the signed-in person's row on a reference to the auth.me table, their email on a text column) — { "auto": "today" } and so on in JSON. Filled in as the form opens, and by the server on a create that leaves them out; a column the form does not show is the server's, whatever a create says. The text "today", "now" or "me" is refused, since it would read as the value filled in. Or { "from": "service_id.price" }: the value of the record a reference names, refreshed as it is chosen until the person edits it, and filled by the server where a create leaves it out. | `resources.*.restocks.message.args` | object | Stable | Each ICU argument's column path: { "title": "thread_id.title" }. |

## `resources.*.rollups`

| Key | Type | Status | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `resources.*.rollups` | object | Stable | Numbers about the rows that point at each record, by name, read like columns wherever a column is (a list's show, a sort, a condition, a command's when, a page's fields, display and labels): count(from), sum, min or max (from, column), or latest (from, column), a column of the newest row. Computed in the record's own statement through the child's grants and row scope; never written. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/resources.ts`. |
| `resources.*.rollups.*.column` | string | Stable | The column of `from` a sum, min, max or latest reads; a count names none. A sum, min or max may read a computed column of `from` that reads only its row's own columns, written inline; a latest reads a stored column of any type, and serves its vocabulary. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/app.ts`. |
| `resources.*.rollups.*.fn` | `"count"` · `"sum"` · `"min"` · `"max"` · `"latest"` | Stable |  One of `count`, `latest`, `max`, `min`, `sum`. |
| `resources.*.rollups.*.from` | string | Stable | The resource whose rows point at this one. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/app.ts`. |
| `resources.*.rollups.*.query` | string | Stable | Which of `from`'s rows count, in the query language over its own columns, its computed columns that read only its own row, and paths through its references to a stored column: "status = open", "sales_order_id.status != cancelled", "breaching = true". A computed column's `now` and `today` are the request's. |
| `resources.*.rollups.*.segment` | string | Stable | One of from's segments: the rows it names are the ones counted, ANDed with query. Used in `examples/apps/tick/app.ts`. |
| `resources.*.rollups.*.sort` | string | Stable | A latest's order: the column of `from`, a date or a number, whose greatest value is the newest row (its key breaks a tie, and a row without one is never newer than a row with one). Its integer key when absent. |
| `resources.*.rollups.*.whose` | string | Stable | The reference on `from` that points here, when there is more than one; or two, `task_id.project_id`, when `from` points at a record that points here. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/resources.ts`. |

## `resources.*.search`

| Key | Type | Status | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `resources.*.search` | object | Preview | Search through a search provider: fields are the columns the index holds, or one step along a reference (requester.name) whose value each document copies and follows; connection names the provider's connection. The list's filter box, reference pickers and the palette ask it and re-read the rows under the reader's grants; while it is down they search the database. Needs a single-column primary key. On a tenant App each document keeps its tenant and a search asks within the member's tenant. Search providers are packs (Typesense is @mistriwork/search-typesense), which ship after 1.0; until one is plugged in, an App that declares search is refused at startup. Used in `examples/apps/tick/app.ts`. |
| `resources.*.search.connection` | string | Preview |  Used in `examples/apps/tick/app.ts`. |
| `resources.*.search.fields` | array | Preview |  Used in `examples/apps/tick/app.ts`. |

## `resources.*.text`

| Key | Type | Status | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `resources.*.text` | object | Stable | How long a text column's value may be and what form it takes, keyed by column: min and max characters and a pattern the whole value matches, with an optional message. The New form says the rule as someone types; the server holds every write to it. On PostgreSQL a varchar(n) and a simple char_length or ~ CHECK give the database's rule free; the App's wins key by key. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/views.ts`. |

| `resources.*.text.*.message` | string | Stable | What the form says when the rule is not met. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/resources.ts`. |

| `resources.*.text.*.pattern` | string | Stable | A JavaScript regular expression the whole value matches. |

| Key | Type | Status | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

## `resources.*.validation[]`

| Key | Type | Status | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `resources.*.validation[].message` | string | Stable | Static plain text. No row-value interpolation. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/resources.ts`. |
| `resources.*.validation[].must` | string | Stable | A condition in the query language, the one a page section's or an action's when speaks: "completed = false", "stage = closed_won and probability &lt; 100", "pay_type in (salary, hourly)", "due_on is empty". Read against the record's own values: local columns compared with =, !=, &lt;, &lt;=, >, >=, in and is (not) empty, joined by and, or and parentheses; no paths, no text matching, at most 16 comparisons. Unknown or uncomparable dependencies stay unresolved. Text and booleans support only = and !=; ordered comparisons require compatible numeric or temporal columns. Used in `examples/apps/lintel/resources.ts`. |
| `resources.*.validation[].when` | string | Stable | A condition in the query language, the one a page section's or an action's when speaks: "completed = false", "stage = closed_won and probability &lt; 100", "pay_type in (salary, hourly)", "due_on is empty". Read against the record's own values: local columns compared with =, !=, &lt;, &lt;=, >, >=, in and is (not) empty, joined by and, or and parentheses; no paths, no text matching, at most 16 comparisons. Unknown or uncomparable dependencies stay unresolved. Text and booleans support only = and !=; ordered comparisons require compatible numeric or temporal columns. Used in `examples/apps/tick/app.ts`. |
